Your companion is a horse, pony, or similar equine.

Size Medium or Large

Melee 1 hoof (agile), Damage 1d6 bludgeoning

Str +3, Dex +2, Con +2, Int –4, Wis +1, Cha +0

Hit Points 8

Skill Survival

Senses low-light vision, scent (imprecise, 30 feet)

Speed 40 feet

Special mount

Support Benefit Until the start of your next turn, if you're mounted on your horse and moved 10 feet or more on the action before a melee Strike, add a circumstance bonus to damage for that Strike equal to twice the number of weapon damage dice. If your weapon already has the jousting weapon trait, increase the trait's damage bonus by 2 per die instead.

Advanced Maneuver @UUID[Compendium.pf2e-animal-companions.AC-Advanced-Maneuvers.Item.tsOaXTRWQvsKTyaL]{Gallop}

The following are the base statistics for a young animal companion, the first animal companion most characters get. You adjust these statistics depending on the type of animal you choose. Animal companions calculate their modifiers and DCs just as you do with one difference: the only item bonuses they can benefit from are to Speed and AC (their maximum item bonus to AC is +3). As you gain levels, you might be able to make your companion stronger by advancing it.

An animal companion's starting statistics are as follows.

  • Level: Your animal companion's level is equal to yours.
  • Proficiencies: Your animal companion is trained in its unarmed attacks, unarmored defense, barding (a type of armor for animals), all saving throws, Perception, Acrobatics, and Athletics. Animal companions can't use abilities that require greater Intelligence, such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} or Decipher Writing, even if trained in the appropriate skill, unless they have a specialization that allows it.
  • Attribute Modifiers: An animal companion begins with base attribute modifiers listed in its stat block.
  • Hit Points: Your animal companion has ancestry Hit Points from its type, plus a number of Hit Points equal to 6 plus its Constitution modifier for each level you have.

Until the start of your next turn, if you're mounted on your horse and moved 10 feet or more on the action before a melee Strike, add a circumstance bonus to damage for that Strike equal to twice the number of weapon damage dice. If your weapon already has the jousting weapon trait, increase the trait's damage bonus by 2 per die instead.

description.gm:
IF YOU ARE A GM READING THIS DO NOT REMOVE THIS EFFECT FROM A PLAYER CHARACTER!

GM Note: Scourge Infection is level 24, it is listed as level 0 in this effect to prevent metagaming as a failsafe if a player finds the effect in the compendium.

This effect exists on tokens specifically for GMs. Players are not able to see it, including the icon on their token. Players should not be able to see the effect ever, don't uncheck the 'Unidentified?' box or click the eye icon on the effects tab of the character's sheet.

Saving Throw: Varies Onset: 2 minutes

Special: A creature cannot recover from the first two stages of Scourge infection on its own. They must be assisted by another creature via @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TC7OcDa7JlWbqMaN]{Treat Disease}. When a creature does so, the infected creature immediately attempts a Will save with a DC equal to the very-hard difficulty DC for their level. On a success, the infected creature must then attempt a Foritude save with a DC equal to the very-hard difficulty DC for their level. On a success, the infected creature's Scourge infection stage is reduced by 1, but Scourge remains in their body (Carrier, Stage 0). Being reexposed to Scourge later causes the formerly infected creature to skip the onset stage of the infection.

Stage 1: (1 day, disease) Scourge hides under the creature's skin, observing. The infection can usually be visually identified by a red outline of the creature's sclera. Whenever a creature infected with Scourge attempts an action that would harm another Scourged creature or otherwise disrupt Scourge itself, they must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:3], disrupting the action on a failure.

Stage 2: (1 month, disease) Scourge takes a greater hold on the body of the creature it is infecting, causing its blood to become viscous with the consistency of honey. The DC to have an action disrupted from stage 1 of the infection increases to a @Check[flat|dc:8]. Additionally, the creature gains resistance to bleeding damage equal to half its level. When the infected creature dies, a Scourgespawn with a level closest to the creature's level erupts from the creature's corpse after one round.

After the duration of stage 2 has passed, the infection remains at stage 2 until activated by Scourge itself, a Scourge Nexus, or another exceptionally powerful Scourged creature. When activated, the infected creature becomes immune to effects that would activate its infection for 24 hours.

Stage 3: (until activated, posession) Scourge begins assimilating the infected creature into the hivemind. The infection loses the disease trait and gains the possession trait. Treat Disease is no longer an applicable method of reducing the stage of the infection, which must be removed via a method of expelling a creature possessing another creature. If the infection would be removed from the infected creature (such as the effects of an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.6llILJtsTPgtYXgx]{Astral} rune), the infection's stage is reduced by 1, rather than expelling Scourge entirely. If the method of removing the posession requires a save, use the infected creature's saving throw modifier, if the effect requires a counteract check, use Scourge's level as the counteract level (24). The creature gains weakness equal to their level to Siccatite and Time. The DC to have an action disrupted from stage 1 of the infection increases to a @Check[flat|dc:13]. The resistance to bleeding damage gained from stage 2 of the infection increases to the infected creature's level. Whenever the posessed creature starts their turn, they must attempt a @Check[flat|dc:16]. On a failure, they are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} by Scourge for their first action for that turn, or their first two actions on a critical failure.

Stage 4: (until activated, posession) The infected creature fully succumbs to the infection, becoming part of Scourge itself. The infected creature becomes immune to bleeding, and becomes permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} by Scourge until the infection's stage is reduced.

Activate 1 (manipulate)

Involuntary jolts and surges of energy move through the drinker's body as it restores normal muscle control. When you drink this elixir, it attempts to counteract each effect that's inflicting the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled} condition on you, using a 2nd-rank counteract and a [[/r 1d20+8 #Counteract]]{+8 counteract modifier}.

Saddlebags come in a pair. Each can hold up to 3 Bulk of items, and the first 1 Bulk of items in each doesn't count against your mount's Bulk limit. The Bulk value given is for saddlebags worn by a mount. If you are carrying or stowing saddlebags, they count as 1 Bulk instead of light Bulk.

This spear-like weapon is used by a mounted creature to deal a great deal of damage.

Bane rune does extra damage to Oozes
This thick club is inset with sharp teeth, typically from a shark, that easily tear flesh. It's the preferred weapon of many Minatan warriors.

Each war saddle is specifically fitted to a mount's body type and has numerous straps that can secure you on your mount. You remain mounted even if you fall @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} until either you or someone else uses an Interact action to unfasten the straps on the saddle. A creature or effect can separate you from your mount by pulling so hard it tears the straps, but to do so, the effect's DC, attack roll, or skill check must exceed 20.

You can manacle someone who is willing or otherwise at your mercy as an exploration activity taking 10-30 seconds depending on the creature's size and how many manacles you apply. A two-legged creature with its legs bound takes a –15-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds, and a two-handed creature with its wrists bound has to succeed at a @Check[flat|dc:5] any time it uses a manipulate action or else that action fails. This DC may be higher depending on how tightly the manacles constrain the hands. A creature bound to a stationary object is immobilized. For creatures with more or fewer limbs, the GM determines what effect manacles have, if any. Freeing a creature from simple manacles requires three successful @Check[thievery|dc:22|traits:action:pick-a-lock] checks.

You contort yourself to [[/act squeeze]]{squeeze} through a space so small you can barely fit through. This action is for exceptionally small spaces; many tight spaces are difficult terrain that you can move through more quickly and without a check.

Critical Success You squeeze through the tight space in 1 minute per 10 feet of squeezing.

Success You squeeze through in 1 minute per 5 feet.

Critical Failure You become stuck in the tight space. While you're stuck, you can spend 1 minute attempting another Acrobatics check at the same DC. Any result on that check other than a critical failure causes you to become unstuck.

Sample Squeeze Tasks

  • Trained space barely fitting your shoulders
  • Master space barely fitting your head

When you affix these simple iron horseshoes to the hooves of an ordinary horse or a quadrupedal animal companion and the animal companion invests them, that creature gains a +5-foot item bonus to its land Speed and a +2 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to High Jump and Long Jump.

In addition, when it Leaps, it can move 5 feet farther if jumping horizontally or 3 feet higher if jumping vertically.

This elixir warms your core and improves your circulation. For 24 hours, you are protected from the effects of severe cold.

When you advance a young animal companion to a mature animal companion:

  • If your companion is Medium or smaller, it grows by one size.
  • Increase its Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, and Wisdom modifiers by 1.
  • Increase its proficiency rank for Perception and all saving throws to expert. Increase its proficiency ranks in Intimidation, Stealth, and Survival to trained, and if it was already trained in one of those skills from its type, increase its proficiency rank in that skill to expert.
  • Increase its unarmed attack damage from one die to two dice (for instance 1d8 to 2d8)

This weapon is a long +1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.OPMzQdM9rZznMGhW]{Lance} with a muzzle built into the pointed tip, allowing the user to fire the chamber after a successful melee attack. A barrel running down the length of the lance allows you to load firearm ammunition into the base of the weapon more easily than it might seem from the design. It takes 2 actions to reload a blast lance.

Activate f command

Trigger You strike a foe with the blast lance

Requirements The blast lance is loaded with a round

Effect You fire a blast of gunpowder through the weapon that deals @Damage[2d8[fire]] damage. The foe must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:18] save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected by the blast of gunpowder and the blast lance misfires and jams.

Success The target takes half the fire damage.

Failure The target takes the full fire damage and is pushed back 5 feet. You can Stride after it, but you must move the same distance and in the same direction.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and is pushed back 10 feet. You can Stride after it, but you must move the same distance and in the same direction.
The nature of this lance is unclear.

Improved Version because of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.x2a3Qb5pWj6Bgu6a]{Battle-Tested Companion}

This magical banner shimmers in a fiery array of reds, oranges, and yellows. The rampant threads catch light in the wind and give the appearance of a blazing flame. Whenever you or an ally within the banner's aura critically succeeds with a Strike, the Strike deals an additional @Damage[1d4[persistent,fire]] damage.

Granted by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.Item.8NtRuNYGiU2iTwgL]{Commander's Banner}

You gain a +1 status bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects. If the origin has the Glorious Banner feat, this bonus increases to +2, and you gain a +1 status bonus to AC, Fortitude saves, and Reflex saves.

A commander needs a battle standard to help guide their allies on the field. You start play with a custom banner that you can use to signal allies when using tactics (see below) or to deploy specific abilities. Your banner can be affixed to a weapon or shield you are wielding, attached to a simple pole or handle and held in one hand, or worn affixed to a pole alongside your backpack. Your banner might be a literal flag or pennant, a decorated fan, a personalized totem, or some other highly visible and item of negligible or light Bulk. Your banner requires customization and influences your allies' morale, so you can have only one banner at a time designated as your commander's banner; designating a new banner or standard as your commander's banner takes 1 minute.

As long as your banner is visible and in your possession, it provides an aura that gives you and all allies in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] a +1 status bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects. You can pause or resume this effect as part of any action you would typically use to stow or retrieve your banner. If your banner is destroyed or stolen, allies currently benefiting from its bonuses become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}. This effect has the aura, emotion, mental, and visual traits.

Some abilities allow you to place your banner in a specialized manner, such as the Commander's Companion and Plant Banner feats. As long as you have placed your banner in this way, any banner abilities originate from your banner's space instead of your own, and you gain the same basic benefits as when it is in your possession. An unattended banner has the base Hardness and Hit Points of a standard item of its type (usually cloth, thin leather, or thin wood) or the Hardness and Hit Points of the object it is affixed to, whichever is greater.

This charm, usually placed on an animal companion's collar, contains a single strand of your hair, as well as one of your animal companion's, creating a link that better transmits emotional cues to a trained psychological assistance animal.

Time itself lands you a hand to traverse terrain.

Each feather token appears to be a simple feather from some exotic bird. The feather's shaft, dipped in gold, bears a single arcane rune. Activating a feather token causes it to transform into another object, which then can be used as normal for that object. Each feather can be activated only once, with most of them permanently becoming the item in their description.

Activate A Interact

When activated, this token transforms into a small sparrow that waits on your finger for you to relay a message up to 1 minute in length, along with the name and rough location of a recipient. The recipient must be someone you have met, and the location must be somewhere you have visited. After receiving the message, the bird flies off to deliver it, traveling at 30 miles per hour and then searching for the target in the location you provided. If the bird finds the target, it moves adjacent to them, your words emanate from the bird, and the bird then flies off and vanishes. The bird also vanishes if it fails to find your target after 10 hours of searching the location you specified.
A Combat Torch. It is reinforced to be wielded as a weapon. Wildly waving this around deals 1 fire splash damage to creatures adjacent to the target, yourself excluded.
